# Independent PSID density workflow control (synthetic, not author data)

input.csv has14 manually specified raw PSID-shaped records;8 satisfy the exact
positive-earner/age36/education cohort. Covers zero earnings, other age with zero
hours, missing/0/98/99 education, repeated log wages, earnings topcoding, negative
log wage and preserved raw birth/marital codes. Source ordinals fix order.

Generated by R4.6.1/stats4.6.1 with no contributed package:

```sh
Rscript examples/mma09p1np/reference.R tests/fixtures/psid_density/input.csv NEW_DIR
```

sample.csv preserves13 ordered source/derived fields; bandwidth.csv holds9
sample-SD/type7/plugin statistics; density.csv holds512 ordered common-grid rows
with three conventional Epanechnikov KDEs at h/2,h,2h. Total2673 primary numeric/
missing cells, including1536 density ordinates. Root tests require no R/original
assets: they run the actual native script, compare R values and independently
reconstruct the sample, bandwidth, kernel sums and actual SVG geometry in Python.

normalization.csv records independent exact-piece Simpson mass1 for all three
continuous KDEs (not a grid renormalization). fft_certificate.csv additionally
records stats::density at65536/262144 points, with bw=halfwidth/sqrt(5) to match
its variance-standardized kernel convention. The secondary bound uses the1.5
Lipschitz constant, padded internal FFT spacing, data binning and both interpolation
steps; it does not relax1e-11 absolute+1e-10 relative primary tolerances. Record
versions.txt with regenerated references; investigate differences, do not widen
bounds or overwrite frozen values to make failures pass.

Original source acquisition/precision/sample contract lives in
examples/mma09p1np/README.md. No author data/program/log or historical RNG is
redistributed. No uncertainty, general KDE command or whole-figure pixel parity.
